videos.script: When a team brings Renata a design question, the fastest help she can give is an answer. {{title}} It is also how she becomes the bottleneck. The team comes back next month with the next question, and the month after that. {{queue}} This lesson is about the other way. Asking before answering. Helping a team reach its own decision. And saying clearly when something is advice and when it is not. {{questions}} Then a design review. Ícaro, a junior developer on Payments, has written his first design document. It retries Pix payouts that failed. Renata starts from the problem, walks every part of the design and asks what happens when it fails. {{review}} One of her comments blocks the design. The others do not, and she says which is which. {{blocking}} Last, how designers are grown. Letting somebody else write the decision record. Designing in pairs, with the junior person holding the pen. And a kata, a practice problem for architects. {{kata}} The measure for all of it is simple to say. How many good decisions get made at Carreto without Renata in the room.
